coverage.evidence: Bare helpers follow target when one is in context, otherwise user (LegacyTemplateHelpers.cs:538, 1458-1490); target is the first argument word with a leading @ removed (ChatMessageHandler.cs:1908-1917, MentionParser.cs:30-31); a capital first letter capitalizes the result unless it is a name (LegacyTemplateHelpers.cs:137-147); a verb pipe picks the singular form unless the subject is they, and with no pipe the token stays as written (LegacyTemplateHelpers.cs:201-233, 1026-1059).

The fallback words are they, them, their, are, were and person (LegacyTemplateHelpers.cs:1433-1456) and fill every grammar key still unset (LegacyTemplateHelpers.cs:613-631); tense falls back to are or were (LegacyTemplateHelpers.cs:629-630).

Lookup is by login at api.pronouns.alejo.io/v1 (AlejoPronounClient.cs:27-28), on Twitch chat only (PronounHydrationHandler.cs:47-49), with a 24-hour cooldown, override skip and save to the User row (PronounResolutionService.cs:30, 65, 69-70, 88-90); set_pronoun finds the set by Name, sets ManualOverride true, and clear or reset sets it false (SetPronounAction.cs:124-158); the action shows as Set pronoun through humanize (stepWords.ts:38-43, text.ts:14-22); the viewer page sends manualOverride true (viewerAccount.ts:114).

Grammar loads the primary pronoun only (LegacyTemplateHelpers.cs:729-762, 939-977); user.pronouns is primary.Subject/alt.Subject when an alt is set (UserPronounDisplay.cs:28-31); for any and other the name, name's, is, was and person are used, and nothing changes without a name (LegacyTemplateHelpers.cs:1026-1081); the seeded words and combos match PronounSeeder.cs:47-231; the labels Your pronouns and Also uses are in viewer/account/i18n/en.json:19-20.

Bare and target pronoun helpers and every verb form use TriggerContexts (Command, EventResponse, Pipeline, Webhook), and the user.* grammar rows use ViewerOwnContexts, which adds Viewer (TemplateHelperRegistry.cs:62-68, 84-88, 746-776); tense uses AllContexts, which includes Timer and Discord but not Viewer (TemplateHelperRegistry.cs:32-40, 217); timer and Discord saves are validated per context and reject unregistered keys (TimerManagementService.cs:50-54, DiscordNotificationConfigService.cs:361-373, TemplateHelperValidator.cs:37-83).

reader_answers.evidence: The helper roles and the verb rule (first form for he and she, second for they) match PronounGrammarSuffixes and ResolveVerbAgreement (LegacyTemplateHelpers.cs:201-233, 1433-1456); the user. and target. sides and the capital rule match LegacyTemplateHelpers.cs:137-147 and 1458-1490.

Pronoun rows are not registered for Timer or Discord, so the validator rejects them there (TemplateHelperRegistry.cs:746-776, TemplateHelperValidator.cs:37-83), while tense is registered in AllContexts (TemplateHelperRegistry.cs:217); a bare helper follows the first argument word or the sender (ChatMessageHandler.cs:1908-1917, LegacyTemplateHelpers.cs:1467-1470).

A verb token without a pipe returns null and is left as typed (LegacyTemplateHelpers.cs:201-233, ITemplateHelperProvider.cs:42); the example outputs match the seeded words (PronounSeeder.cs:82-205) and the name grammar (LegacyTemplateHelpers.cs:1062-1081).

With no saved pronoun, the they/them fallback fills every grammar key (LegacyTemplateHelpers.cs:613-631, 1433-1456) and the verb takes the plural form for they (LegacyTemplateHelpers.cs:1026-1059); a lookup only happens on Twitch chat, and a null result changes nothing (PronounHydrationHandler.cs:47-49, PronounResolutionService.cs:69-70).
